name: Base64 Codec
description: Convert between text and Base64, and switch between the standard and URL-safe variants.

results.outputHint: The result can be copied directly.

hints.input: When encoding, the input is read using the selected encoding; when decoding, whitespace and padding are ignored.
hints.padding: Turn it off to omit the 「=」 padding, which is common for URLs and file names.
hints.convert: Variant conversion rewrites a Base64 string in the other alphabet; 「Auto-detect」 infers the source variant from the characters used.
hints.output: The decoded output can be rendered as UTF-8 text or hexadecimal.
hints.reverse: Feeds the current result back in and flips the direction, so standard ⇄ URL-safe takes a single click.

faq.a: No. Base64 is only an encoding and anyone can reverse it. Do not use it to protect sensitive data.

faq.q: Why does decoding report invalid input?
faq.a: The input contains characters outside the selected variant or has an invalid length. Check whether the data uses the standard or URL-safe variant.

faq.q: What is the difference between the standard and URL-safe variants?
faq.a: Both encode the same bytes; only the 62nd and 63rd characters differ: 「+」 and 「/」 in the standard alphabet, 「-」 and 「_」 in the URL-safe one. The latter can be dropped straight into URLs, file names and cookie values.

faq.q: Does variant conversion decode the Base64 first?
faq.a: No. The conversion happens at the byte level: the bytes are read with the source variant and re-encoded with the target variant, so nothing is lost in between.
